title: What Happens to Your Money When a Bank Fails? 🏦 #shorts
description:
In March 2023, customers tried to pull $42 billion out of Silicon Valley Bank in one day, and it was shut down the next. In the US, the F-D-I-C insures deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per bank, and no one has lost a cent of insured money since it began in 1934.
Source: FDIC.gov (deposit insurance & "When a Bank Fails"); U.S. Bank Financial IQ; Fortune & Bloomberg (Mar 11, 2023); CNBC (Mar 28, 2023). Education, not financial advice.
script: In March twenty twenty-three, people tried to pull forty-two billion dollars out of one bank in a single day.
The next day, Silicon Valley Bank was shut down.
So what happens to your money when a bank fails?
In America, the F-D-I-C insures your deposits up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars, per person, per bank.
Since that insurance began in nineteen thirty-four, no one has lost a single cent of insured money.
But most of the money at Silicon Valley Bank sat above that limit, in big company accounts.
So know the limit before you ever need it.
